name: Scalp serums, decoded
tagline: What they can do for density, shedding and scalp health, and what they can't.
image_alt: Fingertips resting along a curly hairline, the other hand on the crown.
description: Scalp serums for hair density, shedding and scalp health: what's normal shedding, which ingredients have real evidence (minoxidil, caffeine, rosemary, peptides), how to apply a serum, and when to see a dermatologist.
intro: Scalp serums promise fuller hair, less shedding and a healthier scalp. Some ingredients have real research behind them, and some have mostly marketing. This guide sorts the two, shows you how to use a serum so it has a fair chance, and tells you when it's time to see a dermatologist instead.

causes.title: First, what are you actually seeing?
causes.intro: Shedding, thinning and breakage look alike in the drain. They need different things.
items: Everyday shedding
Losing 50 to 100 hairs a day is normal.
In curly and coily hair, shed hairs stay caught until you detangle, so wash day can look like a lot more than it is.
A shedding spell
More hair than usual falling out all over, often two to four months after a big stressor: illness, giving birth, major weight loss, stress or a new medicine.
It usually settles once the trigger has passed, and fullness tends to return within six to nine months.
Gradual thinning
A wider part or a thinner crown, slowly, over months or years.
Often pattern hair loss. This is where a serum, or a medicine like minoxidil, can help.
Breakage
Short pieces of hair, not full strands with a small white bulb at one end.
That's the strand snapping, not the scalp shedding. A serum won't fix it; conditioning and gentler handling will.
Thinning that comes with pain, bumps or itch
At the edges after tight styles, or at the crown with tenderness or scaling.
Traction alopecia and CCCA are common in Black women and can scar if they're left. See a dermatologist early.

routine.title: Five steps to a scalp routine that's worth it
routine.intro: Do them in order. Each one gives the next a fairer chance.

washes.title: The routine
steps: Start with a calm, clean scalp
A serum only works on skin it can reach. Wash often enough that oil, flakes and product don't sit on your scalp, and settle any flaking or itch before you add something new.

steps.dek: No serum outworks a flaky, itchy scalp.
steps.quote: Treat the scalp first. The serum comes second.

blocks.title: Anti-flake ingredients to look for in a shampoo
items: Ketoconazole
Zinc Pyrithione
Piroctone Olamine
Salicylic Acid

blocks.text: In small studies, anti-dandruff shampoos with ketoconazole, piroctone olamine or zinc pyrithione also cut shedding a little over six months of use. If you flake, they're worth a place on wash day.

deeper.title: When flakes aren't dryness
deeper.sub: Buildup, seborrheic dermatitis, and why oil can make it worse

blocks.text: Waxy, product-coloured flakes that come back days after washing are often buildup. A clarifying wash, then a conditioner for slip, usually clears them.

Greasy yellow scale, redness or itching that won't settle can be seborrheic dermatitis. More oil feeds it rather than fixing it. An anti-dandruff shampoo two or three times a week is the usual first step; a dermatologist can suggest a stronger one.

steps.lockin: Calm and clean before you add anything new.
steps.image_alt: Washing coily hair at a bathroom sink, lather worked into the scalp with fingertips.

steps: Choose a serum by what's in it

Most serums for density lean on the same handful of ingredients. The research behind them ranges from a medicine with decades of trials to an oil with none, so read the label before you trust the front of the bottle.

blocks.title: Scalp ingredients, by the strength of the evidence
blocks.key: More filled bars means stronger research in people, not a better product for you.

tiers.label: Medicine
tiers.note: Approved to treat pattern hair loss. Sold with dosing directions, not as a cosmetic.
items: Minoxidil
The only over-the-counter medicine approved for pattern hair loss in women and men, as a 2% solution or a 5% foam.
Extra shedding in the first weeks is common and usually passes. Results take at least four months, and stop when you stop using it.

tiers.label: Some trials in people
tiers.note: Promising, but small, short or funded by the maker.
items: Caffeine
In a 2017 trial of 210 men, a 0.2% caffeine liquid did about as well as 5% minoxidil at keeping hairs in their growing phase.
One trial, in men, run with the maker. Promising, not proven.
Ketoconazole
An anti-dandruff ingredient that improved hair density in small studies, mostly as a shampoo.
Easiest to use as your wash-day shampoo, two or three times a week.
Rosemary oil
In a 2015 trial of 100 people, rosemary oil matched 2% minoxidil after six months, with less scalp itch.
It was compared with the weaker strength of minoxidil, and neither group had changed by month three.
Pumpkin seed oil
In a 2021 trial of 60 women with pattern thinning, pumpkin seed oil improved hair over three months.
Small and short. Worth watching, not betting on.

tiers.label: Mostly the maker's own studies
tiers.note: Common in density serums. Independent trials of each one on its own are scarce.
items: Redensyl
A plant complex aimed at density, often with a green-tea-derived ingredient.
Capixyl
A peptide with red clover extract, for fuller-looking hair.
Procapil
A peptide with apigenin and oleanolic acid. Often sold together with the two above.
Aminexil
L'Oréal's anti-hair-fall ingredient. It is not minoxidil, despite the similar name.

tiers.label: Comfort, not growth
tiers.note: Nice to use. No good evidence they add hair.
items: Castor oil
Loved for shine and slip on the lengths, but no human trials show it grows hair.
Scalp massage
In a 2016 study of nine men, four minutes a day for 24 weeks made hairs a little thicker.
Tiny study, but free, and it helps a serum spread. Keep it gentle on braids and edges.

blocks.label: Serums built on these ingredients
use: The INKEY List Caffeine Stimulating Scalp Treatment
L'Oréal Paris Elvive Fall Resist Aminexil Serum
1.5% Aminexil with caffeine. Full Resist in the UK.
California Naturals Re:GRO Anti-Thinning Scalp Serum

deeper.title: How to read a serum label

blocks.text: A percentage on the front tells you how much of the star ingredient is in there. With no percentage, look for it in the first half of the ingredient list.
Fragrance and essential oils, rosemary included, are common causes of scalp irritation. If your scalp is sensitive, start with a fragrance-free formula.
Put a little behind your ear or on your inner arm for two days before it goes on your whole scalp.

steps.lockin: Pick one serum for its evidence, not its hype, and stick with it.
steps.image_alt: Hands holding a dropper bottle of a multi-peptide hair density serum against dark wood.

steps: Put it on your scalp, not your hair
A serum does nothing on the lengths. Part your hair into sections, apply along each part, and massage it in with your fingertips. Follow the label for how much and how often.

steps.dek: Small amounts, right on the skin, every time.
steps.quote: The same few drops every day beat a big dose once in a while.

blocks.title: How to apply
items: 1. Start right
On a clean scalp, dry or towel-dried, as the label says.
2. Part
Make a part about an inch from your hairline.
3. Apply
A few drops along the part, right on the skin.
4. Repeat
Move over an inch and do it again until the area is covered.
5. Massage
Fingertips, not nails, for a minute or two.
6. Let it dry
Before you style, tie your hair up or sleep.

blocks.title: More isn't faster.
paras: Extra drops don't add results. They add buildup and a higher chance of irritation.

items: Braids, locs and twists
A nozzle bottle or dropper along the parts. Lighter, water-based serums leave less buildup.
Loose hair
Work in sections so the serum reaches skin, not just the hair on top.

steps.lockin: On the scalp, in sections, on schedule.
steps.note: Burning, redness or new itching after you apply? Rinse it off and stop using it.
steps.image_alt: Neat cornrows with clear parts, braids hanging over one shoulder.

steps: Give it time, and track it
Hair grows slowly, so every serum needs months. Plan on three to four months of steady use before you judge it, and up to a year for the full picture.

steps.dek: Week two is too early to know anything.

blocks.title: What to expect
items: Weeks 1 to 8
Nothing to see yet. With minoxidil, some extra shedding is common.
Months 3 to 4
The first fair check: less shedding, fine new hairs along your part.
Month 6
A good point to decide whether it's working for you.
Month 12
The full result.

blocks.text: Take the same photo every month
Same light, same spot, same part, hair dry. Your memory will tell you nothing has changed; photos won't.

steps.lockin: Judge it at month four, not week two.
steps.image_alt: A full, rounded coily wash and go, seen from the side.

steps: Ease the tension, and check what's underneath
A serum can't undo hair pulled out by tight styles, and shedding often starts somewhere else in the body. Loosen what pulls, and get checked if shedding won't settle.

steps.dek: Your scalp is part of the rest of you.

blocks.title: Signs a style is too tight
items: Pain or tenderness after styling
Your scalp shouldn't hurt in a fresh style. If it does, take it down or loosen it.
Small bumps along the hairline
A sign of pulling at the follicle.
Thinning where the tension sits
Edges, temples or around the parts of braids and ponytails.

blocks.text: Iron and ferritin, vitamin D and thyroid are common checks when shedding won't stop. Bring a list of recent illness, new medicines and stress.
A dermatologist can tell shedding from pattern loss, traction alopecia or CCCA. For the kinds that scar, the sooner the better.

steps.lockin: Loosen what pulls. Check what's underneath.
steps.note: Patches, tenderness, bumps or itching at the crown? See a dermatologist soon.
steps.image_alt: Cornrows braided back from the hairline into long braids.

track: Log each application and a monthly scalp photo, so your month-four check is an honest one.

trouble.title: If something feels off
items: My scalp itches or burns after a serum
Stop using it. Fragrance, essential oils, alcohol and propylene glycol are common irritants. Try a fragrance-free formula, or ask a dermatologist.
More shedding after starting minoxidil
Common in the first weeks and usually temporary. If it carries on past three months, check in with a doctor.
Buildup under braids or locs
Use less, choose a lighter water-based formula, and wash your scalp every week or two.
Hair coming out in clumps or patches
See a dermatologist. Patches aren't everyday shedding.
No change after six months
Talk to a dermatologist about other options, and ask about blood tests.

end.title: The scalp serum lock-in
notes: A serum is a slow habit, not a quick fix.
Healthy scalp first, the right ingredient second, patience third.
